clue.text: Rocket engineer

parts.note: reads like someone building spacecraft, but Rocket was the famous early steam locomotive of 1829

explanation.surface: A space-age rocket scientist.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue invites thoughts of space flight; the Rocket was the Stephensons' pioneering railway locomotive, which won the Rainhill Trials.
explanation.definitionFit: George and Robert Stephenson designed and built the steam locomotive called Rocket.

clue.text: Happen to see bird nesting as resident

indicators.note: a bird nesting sits inside, so one word goes within the other here

parts.note: to happen is to occur
a pie is a magpie, an old word for the bird

explanation.surface: Someone sees a bird nesting near where they live.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is one who occupies a place, an inhabitant of a house.

clue.text: Remarks we're not supposed to hear when the team comes in

definitions.text: Remarks we're not supposed to hear

indicators.note: the team comes in, entering the middle of the other word

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Whispered comments made as the team walks onto the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Asides in theatre are remarks spoken for the audience that other characters supposedly cannot hear.

clue.text: Left in charge

explanation.definitionFit: Over means remaining as in 'left over', and also in authority, as in 'over the staff'.

clue.text: Short races organised for play groups

indicators.note: organised means arranged anew, so the letters are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Brief running races are set up for preschool play groups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play groups' suggests nurseries for toddlers; it means groups who play music.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestras are ensembles of players, groups who play instruments together.

clue.text: It is inclined to lie low when troubles intervene

indicators.note: troubles intervene by coming between, so they sit within the other word

parts.note: to lie low is to hide
ills are troubles or misfortunes

explanation.surface: Someone tends to keep a low profile when trouble comes along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It is inclined' sounds like a person's tendency; it literally means a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A hillside is sloping ground, something tilted or on an incline.

clue.text: Very nervous near the brink

definitions.meaning: literally close to the edge of something

explanation.definitionFit: On edge means anxious and tense, and literally positioned at the brink or rim.

clue.text: Wear down in fight

definitions.meaning: of fabric, to unravel at the edges through use

explanation.definitionFit: Cloth frays as it wears thin, and a fray is a noisy fight or skirmish.

clue.text: Just keeps going when credit's no longer available

parts.note: tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick; with 's it reads 'credit is'
over means finished, ended

explanation.surface: Someone carries on when the shop stops letting them pay later.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as a sentence: 'tick's over', credit is finished. TICK is British slang for credit.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over runs idling, so something ticking over is merely keeping going.

clue.text: Private hotel used by monarch

parts.note: an inn is a small hotel
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A private hotel patronised by a king or queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts are private ones, kept within and not shared.

clue.text: Sack and what may be put in it

definitions.meaning: a verb, to loot or pillage a town

definitions.text: what may be put in it
definitions.meaning: booty, the loot carried off in a sack

explanation.definitionFit: To plunder is to sack a town, and plunder is also the loot one might stuff into a sack.

clue.text: Time to be off

parts.note: sounds like a signal to leave, but means a period of being off work

explanation.surface: A cue to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A holiday is a period away from work, leave or vacation.

clue.text: Lives wildly, producing social problems

indicators.note: wildly suggests letters scattered out of order

explanation.surface: A reckless lifestyle leads to troubles in society.
explanation.definitionFit: Evils are harmful things, the social ills or wrongs of a community.

clue.text: Sober sailor directed to carry the can

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: one word carries another inside it

parts.note: sent means directed or dispatched
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A teetotal seaman is ordered to take the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carry the can' is a British idiom for taking the blame, a misdirection here.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sober and abstinent refrains from drinking alcohol.

clue.text: No cause for rejoicing when standards are this low

definitions.text: No cause for rejoicing when standards are this low

parts.words: No cause for rejoicing when standards are this low
parts.note: standards are flags, not levels of quality; flags lowered partway signal mourning

explanation.surface: Falling standards are nothing to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Flags flown halfway down the pole mark a death, a sign of mourning.

clue.text: Having a little nap on a bed rather naughtily

indicators.note: acting naughtily means misbehaving, so the letters fall out of line

explanation.surface: Snoozing on someone's bed is a bit cheeky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nap' is not a doze but the raised pile on cloth; a worn garment has only a little left.
explanation.definitionFit: Threadbare fabric is worn so thin that hardly any nap, or pile, remains on it.

clue.text: He picks up the litter

parts.note: suggests a street cleaner, but a litter here is a stretcher for carrying the wounded

explanation.surface: A man collecting rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A litter is an old word for a stretcher, which this bearer lifts and carries.

clue.text: Dates and removes

definitions.meaning: goes out with, escorts on a date

explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone out means dating them, and taking something out means removing it.

clue.text: Submitted and faced the wall

definitions.meaning: handed in, as a bill or report
coated with plaster or cement render

explanation.definitionFit: A rendered account is one submitted, and a rendered wall has been given a plaster facing.

clue.text: Miners' union heads who are stupid

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British coal miners' union
skulls are heads

explanation.surface: The leaders of the miners' union are fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Numskulls are dimwits, people who are dense or foolish; the clue gives a descriptive phrase for them.

clue.text: Limited in one's outlook

parts.note: reads as narrow-minded, but also literally short-sighted in vision

explanation.surface: Narrow-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Short-sighted eyes see only near things, and figuratively a short-sighted person lacks foresight.

clue.text: Sail Columbus raised here

definitions.meaning: a large jib sail on a yacht
the Italian port city where Christopher Columbus grew up

explanation.definitionFit: A genoa is a big foresail, and Genoa is the Italian city where Columbus was born and raised.

clue.text: Does the writing for another Ibsen play

definitions.meaning: writes books credited to someone else

explanation.definitionFit: A ghostwriter ghosts a book for someone else, and Ibsen wrote a play of that title.

clue.text: Flotilla leader almost wrecked — some debris seen

indicators.note: the leader of the flotilla is its opening letter
wrecked suggests something broken up and reassembled differently

explanation.surface: The lead boat of a small fleet is nearly sunk, and wreckage is spotted.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating wreckage from a ship is called flotsam, a kind of debris.

clue.text: Air traffic control in a state of panic

definitions.meaning: a hinged surface on an aircraft wing that controls its movement through the air

explanation.definitionFit: A wing flap is a control surface on aircraft, and being in a flap means being agitated.

clue.text: Saw dog's name inside lead

indicators.note: the dog's name goes inside the symbol for lead

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Rover is a traditional name for a dog

explanation.surface: A dog's name is engraved inside its lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun, an old saying, not the past tense of see or a tool; 'lead' is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional saying or maxim, the same as a proverb.

clue.text: They went to market on foot

definitions.text: They went to market on foot

parts.words: They went to market on foot
parts.note: recalls the nursery rhyme 'This little piggy went to market', counted on a child's toes

explanation.surface: Shoppers walking to the market.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'This little piggy went to market' is played on a child's toes, so the piggies are on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: In the nursery rhyme the little piggies go to market, each one a toe of the foot.

clue.text: Farewell notice that is given to union leader

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: the leader of union is its first letter

explanation.surface: A goodbye notice is handed to the head of a trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieu is a French word for goodbye, used in English as a farewell.

clue.text: Seeing sense a prophet becomes a tourist

parts.note: sight is the sense of seeing
a seer is a prophet

explanation.surface: A visionary prophet takes up sightseeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourist goes around viewing the sights, which is what a sightseer does.
